what: Turn-limit cases, held by both languages so the helm and the resolver cannot drift.
why: The client re-implements the resolver's turn ceiling because a compass has to be drawn before
any round trip returns. That second implementation is allowed to exist only because this file
holds it to the first: `movement.test.ts` runs every case against `maxLegalTurn`, and
Change either implementation and one of the two suites goes red.
The case that made this file necessary: a ship at rest that is not accelerating rotates to any
heading for free. The resolver carved that out by name in MaxTurnSteps and again in Validate;
the client had no copy, so the compass capped a stationary ship at half thrust and the map
refused the rotation with 'has no turn points left'.

cases.name: under way, no velocity change, even thrust
under way, no velocity change, odd thrust rounds up
under way, accelerating, thrust binds before the half-thrust cap
under way, all thrust spent on acceleration
under way, more acceleration than thrust never goes below zero
under way, decelerating, the sign does not matter
under way with no thrust cannot turn
at rest and not accelerating rotates a full circle
at rest with no thrust entered still rotates - the state every new ship is created in
at rest but accelerating is an ordinary move again
at rest but accelerating hard spends the thrust
